articles.title: New York State Gets One More Shot at Opportunity Zones
articles.narrative: This article discusses the revised Opportunity Zone (OZ) program, highlighting its resilience in attracting capital for ground-up development even when conventional equity retreated. The author argues that OZ capital's mandatory 10-year investment horizon and tax-advantaged pricing make it suitable for emerging neighborhoods. With Congress having rewritten the program, New York State has a 60-day window to designate new OZ tracts, which now require a median family income at or below 70% of AMI and eliminate the contiguous tract provision. The author, an equity investments head at a major real estate firm, advises local leaders to identify eligible tracts, assemble investable projects, and demonstrate predictable approval processes to effectively direct this capital to areas most in need.

articles.title: Prosper and Versluys Close $50M Land Deal for $650M Miami Condo Tower
articles.narrative: A joint venture between Prosper Group and Versluys Group has acquired a 1-acre development site in Miami's Brickell district for $50 million, with plans to construct a 60-story, 181-unit luxury condominium tower. The project, estimated to cost $650 million, marks the Belgian developer Versluys Group's first venture into the U.S. market. The acquisition was financed with a $30.5 million loan from Vaster.

data_points.notable_features: Waterfront site with over 300 feet of water frontage along the Miami River, near the Brickell City Center mixed-use complex.
data_points.project_notes: The acquisition includes three parcels, two of which are adjacent inland spots. The site was under contract for at least eight months.

articles.title: Brookfield Asset Management Raises Record $77B in Q2
articles.narrative: Brookfield Asset Management reported a record-breaking second quarter in 2026, raising $77 billion and increasing its assets under management to over $1 trillion. The firm deployed $21 billion during the quarter, including significant capital into its private equity and infrastructure funds, which are on track to be the largest of their vintages. Brookfield also secured $5 billion for its inaugural AI Infrastructure Fund and expanded its financing framework with Bloom Energy to $25 billion for AI infrastructure power projects. On the real estate side, the firm raised $4.3 billion and deployed $5.2 billion, acquiring a U.S. manufactured-home portfolio and an outdoor industrial storage portfolio.

articles.title: Return-to-Office Gained New Momentum in First Half of 2026: Report
articles.narrative: A new report indicates that U.S. office attendance gained momentum in the first half of 2026, with visits rising 6 percent year-over-year and achieving the narrowest gap from pre-pandemic levels to date. However, the return-to-office trend shows significant regional divergence, with markets like Miami and New York nearing baseline visitation while Denver and Chicago lag considerably. The report suggests that while hybrid work remains prevalent, its popularity may be waning in some areas, and the increasing number of companies mandating office attendance could further shift dynamics in the latter half of the year.

articles.title: Krea USA Nabs $62M Construction Loan for Lauderhill, Fla., Rental
articles.narrative: Krea USA secured a $61.8 million construction loan from Abanca Bank for its 385-unit multifamily development, Le Parc at Lauderhill, in Lauderhill, FL. The project, which broke ground in March and is slated for completion next year, will feature three eight-story buildings on a 10-acre site. Although initially planned as workforce housing, the development will now have no rental restrictions, but will retain a $9.1 million tax abatement from the City of Lauderhill.

data_points.notable_features: Includes a day care operated by a nonprofit; rents expected to range between 100% and 120% of area median income.
data_points.project_notes: Project underwent changes from its original 2020 vision as workforce housing; a $9.1 million tax abatement over 10 years, approved in 2022, remains in effect; developer will build a public road.

articles.title: Lee & Associates’ Q2 Report: Office, Retail Markets Gain Momentum as Industrial, Multifamily Face Headwinds
articles.narrative: Lee & Associates' Q2 2026 North America Market Report indicates a varied recovery across commercial real estate sectors. The office and retail markets are gaining momentum, with office experiencing its best year since the pandemic, marked by declining vacancies and increased investor confidence in premium assets. Conversely, the industrial sector faces uneven demand due to trade uncertainties and a supply overhang, leading to a slight increase in vacancy rates and slowed rent growth. Multifamily fundamentals are stabilizing as new supply moderates, while investors and occupiers across all property types remain highly selective in an evolving market.
articles.market_intelligence: Leading industrial markets in net absorption over the past 12 months include Dallas-Fort Worth (28.7M SF), Phoenix (23.5M SF), Houston (18.3M SF), Indianapolis (15.5M SF), and Columbus (12.7M SF). Markets with the least empty industrial space at the end of Q2 2026 were Cleveland (4.4%), Detroit (4.9%), Chicago (5.4%), Pittsburgh (5.5%), St. Louis (5.5%), Columbus (6.4%), Los Angeles (6.5%), and Orange County (6.5%). Markets with the highest industrial vacancy rates include Austin (14.3%), San Francisco (12.5%), Phoenix (10.5%), Seattle (10.1%), and Charlotte (9.8%). Office markets surging include New York City, Dallas, Austin, Houston, San Francisco, and San Jose.

articles.title: University of St. Thomas Breaks Ground on 400-Bed Residence Hall Project in Houston
articles.narrative: The University of St. Thomas has commenced construction on a new 400-bed residence hall within its Houston campus. This 95,000-square-foot development will feature a dedicated chapel, prayer room, courtyard, multi-use lounges, and collaborative study areas. The units will offer various bedroom configurations, including two-, three-, and four-bedroom layouts, designed for single or double occupancy, along with two staff apartments.

data_points.notable_features: Includes a dedicated chapel and prayer room, courtyard, multi-use lounges, and collaborative study zones. Units will be offered in two-, three-, and four-bedroom configurations for single or double occupancy, plus two staff apartments.
data_points.project_notes: Tentative completion date was not announced.

articles.title: Lindenmeyr Munroe Signs 100,043 SF Industrial Lease in North Houston
articles.narrative: Lindenmeyr Munroe, a distributor of printing and packaging paper, has signed a 100,043-square-foot industrial lease at Building 3 of Patriot Business Park in North Houston. The property is a newly constructed, three-building development. Stream Realty Partners represented the landlord, a partnership between Investment & Development Ventures and Standard Real Estate Investments, while Cushman & Wakefield represented the tenant.

data_points.project_notes: Formerly known as Veterans Memorial Business Park.

articles.title: Lee & Associates Negotiates 56,780 SF Industrial Lease in Grand Prairie, Texas
articles.narrative: Lee & Associates has brokered a 56,780-square-foot industrial lease in Grand Prairie, Texas. The transaction involved an undisclosed tenant and an anonymous landlord for a property located at 2401 W. Marshall Drive. The building, constructed in 1966, totals 320,366 square feet.

data_points.address: 2401 W. Marshall Drive, Grand Prairie, TX

articles.title: Making affordable housing more affordable to build
articles.narrative: This article argues that early collaboration and strategic planning during the preconstruction phase are crucial for making affordable housing developments more cost-effective and efficient. The author, drawing on experience as a general contractor, emphasizes that engaging the construction team early allows for better constructability evaluations, more efficient system recommendations, and proactive identification of logistical challenges, ultimately reducing costs and risks. Strong partnerships among owners, architects, contractors, and other stakeholders, along with thoughtful procurement strategies, are also highlighted as key factors in successfully delivering affordable housing projects within tight budgets and schedules.

articles.title: The NRP Group marks groundbreaking of 336-unit multifamily community in Columbus
articles.narrative: The NRP Group has broken ground on OSU East, a 336-unit market-rate multifamily community in Northwest Columbus, Ohio. This project marks the developer's first market-rate community in the city and is situated on a 27.5-acre site that will also include 138 for-sale townhomes by M/I Homes. The development is strategically located near major employment centers, transit corridors, and amenities, addressing the strong demand for high-quality rental housing in a rapidly growing residential corridor. The project is supported by equity from Carlyle Group and financing from PNC Bank, with the City of Columbus acting as a key partner.

data_points.notable_features: Located near Ohio State University Airport and within the Worthington School District, offering proximity to Dublin's employment and lifestyle hubs. Features include a clubhouse, fitness center, coworking space, resort-style pool, and an 11-foot-wide bike path along the frontage.
data_points.project_notes: The 27.5-acre site will also include 138 for-sale townhomes developed by M/I Homes of Central Ohio LLC, with their construction expected to begin in spring 2027.

articles.title: CBL Properties, Greystar celebrate groundbreaking of mixed-use development in Franklin
articles.narrative: CBL Properties and Greystar have broken ground on a new mixed-use development at CoolSprings Galleria in Franklin, TN. The project will add 361 residential units and approximately 15,000 square feet of new retail and restaurant space to the existing campus. This development is part of the ongoing evolution of CoolSprings Galleria, aiming to create a vibrant mixed-use environment that complements the area's character and supports the growth of Franklin and Williamson County.

data_points.notable_features: Located within the CoolSprings Galleria campus, designed to reflect the architectural heritage of Franklin.
data_points.project_notes: The 5.35-acre parcel of underutilized parking was previously sold by CBL Properties to Greystar in June 2026 for this development.

articles.title: Northmarq leads sale and acquisition financing for 190-unit multifamily community in Jeffersonville
articles.narrative: Northmarq's investment sales and debt & equity teams facilitated the sale and acquisition financing of Jeff on 10th, a 190-unit multifamily community in Jeffersonville, Indiana. The property, built in 2022, was sold by a regional multifamily developer to S&S Properties Investment. Northmarq also arranged permanent-fixed financing for the buyer through its Fannie Mae DUS platform, structured on a seven-year term.

data_points.notable_features: The community offers a resort-style swimming pool, 24-hour fitness center, outdoor grilling areas, community fire pits, a conference center, and a 24-hour pet spa. It is located near major employers and economic drivers including the 6,000-acre River Ridge campus.

articles.title: NAI Wisinski brokers sale of historic commercial building in Grand Rapids
articles.narrative: NAI Wisinski of West Michigan brokered the sale of a 4,320-square-foot historic commercial building at 336 Hall Street SE in Grand Rapids, MI. The property, owned by Cal Jen LLC for over a decade, was acquired by a local organization that plans to convert it into a nonprofit community center. The transaction faced challenges due to the City of Grand Rapids' redevelopment plans for an adjacent parking lot, which impacted the property's value and required a revised marketing strategy to highlight alternative solutions like converting a rear garden into parking.

data_points.address: 336 Hall Street SE, Grand Rapids, MI
data_points.project_notes: The City of Grand Rapids' redevelopment plans for an adjacent library-owned parking lot eliminated it as a long-term parking option for the property, impacting its value and requiring a revised marketing strategy.

articles.title: Hawkins Way, Varde Acquire East Village Student Housing
articles.narrative: Hawkins Way Capital and Varde Partners have acquired an East Village student housing property for $28 million, expanding their FOUND Study portfolio in Manhattan. The off-market transaction adds a property with apartment-style layouts, offering flexibility for both student housing and conventional multifamily use. This acquisition aligns with the joint venture's strategy to invest in urban student housing assets in high-demand areas with strong real estate fundamentals and proximity to major universities.

data_points.address: 81 E. 3rd St., New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Apartment-style layouts offering flexible use for student housing or conventional multifamily; located in Manhattan's East Village near leading universities.
data_points.project_notes: Acquired off-market as a strategic addition to the FOUND Study student housing portfolio.

articles.title: Former Blue Shield of CA Offices Trade for Residential Conversion
articles.narrative: The Olson Company acquired a 7.9-acre office campus in Monterey Park, CA, for $24.85 million, with plans to redevelop the site into a new residential community. The campus, which includes two office buildings totaling 120,191 square feet, was formerly owned and occupied by Blue Shield of California. This transaction highlights a growing trend of converting well-located, underutilized office properties into housing in the San Gabriel Valley, addressing the region's demand for new residential units.

data_points.address: 601 Potrero Grande Dr. and 2100 Saturn St., Monterey Park, CA
data_points.notable_features: Former office campus to be redeveloped into a residential community.
data_points.project_notes: The property was previously owned and occupied by Blue Shield of California.

articles.title: JAMS Relocating New York Offices to 3 Times Square
articles.narrative: JAMS, a provider of alternative dispute resolution services, has signed an 11-year lease to relocate its New York Resolution Center to 3 Times Square. The company will occupy 55,335 square feet across the top two floors of the building, with plans to move from its current offices at 620 Eighth Ave. in the fourth quarter of 2027. This significant commitment highlights the ongoing demand for high-quality, well-located office properties in Midtown Manhattan that offer premier amenities and excellent transit connectivity.

data_points.address: 3 Times Square, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Located in Midtown Manhattan with premier amenity programs and transit connectivity.
data_points.project_notes: JAMS is relocating from its current offices at 620 Eighth Ave.

articles.title: Shopoff Sells Site of Proposed Newport Beach Condo Development
articles.narrative: Shopoff Realty Investments has sold the 1.06-acre Park Palm site, entitled for 23 townhomes, to Shea Homes. The property is part of Shopoff's larger Uptown Newport Village master-planned community in Newport Beach, which the firm acquired in 2010 and subsequently entitled for a mixed-use residential village. This sale will complete Phase I of the master plan, with construction on the townhomes expected to begin in 2027.

data_points.phase_1: Park Palm will round out Phase I
data_points.project_notes: Site is part of the 25-acre Uptown Newport Village master-planned community, which was acquired by Shopoff in December 2010 and entitled in 2013 for 1,244 residential units, 11,500 SF of commercial/retail space, and two one-acre parks.

articles.title: JLL Lists Staten Island Waterfront Development for $45M
articles.narrative: JLL Capital Markets has been retained by Triangle Equities as the sales advisor for Lighthouse Point, a newly completed, transit-oriented, Class A multifamily waterfront development in Staten Island. The property, which features 115 residential units, is being marketed for $45 million. The project is considered a rare opportunity in a market with limited new development, offering both quality construction and future potential.

data_points.notable_features: Mixed-use development situated adjacent to the Staten Island Ferry Terminal, occupying the site of the historic U.S. Lighthouse Service’s General Depot.

articles.title: CRE Leaders Stress Importance Of Adaptability As DFW Continues To Grow
articles.narrative: The Dallas-Fort Worth commercial real estate market is experiencing significant growth, prompting industry leaders to emphasize the critical need for adaptability. This expansion is also marked by a notable increase in female leadership within the sector, highlighting a shift in the demographic landscape of the region's CRE industry.

data_points.notable_features: Rising female leadership in the CRE sector.

articles.title: Chicago's Apartment Pipeline Is Slowing, But This Lender Bets On Rehab Instead
articles.narrative: Community Investment Corporation (CIC) has a long history of financing the rehabilitation of multifamily properties in Chicago. Since 1984, the organization has provided approximately 2,800 loans, totaling $1.8 billion, to support the renovation of nearly 70,000 apartment units. This focus on existing stock comes as the new apartment development pipeline in Chicago is reportedly slowing.

articles.title: Elon Musk's Space Data Center Vision Collides With Wall Street's Bottom-Line Reality
articles.narrative: SpaceX's recent post-IPO earnings report has raised concerns among Wall Street analysts regarding the company's short-term artificial intelligence expenditures. The market is scrutinizing the financial implications of Elon Musk's ambitious vision to develop space-based data centers, questioning the immediate returns on these significant investments.

articles.title: HUD Withholds Voucher Funding, Pushing Landlords, Tenants To The Brink
articles.narrative: The Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) has reportedly withheld funding for emergency housing vouchers, creating significant uncertainty for both tenants relying on these subsidies and landlords who accept them. This action is placing financial strain on vulnerable populations and potentially impacting the stability of rental housing providers.

articles.title: $1.1B Loan To Hudson Pacific, Blackstone Moves To Special Servicing
articles.narrative: A $1.1 billion loan secured by a portfolio of Hudson Pacific Properties and Blackstone assets has been transferred to special servicing. The move comes as the borrowers are working to finalize agreed-upon loan extensions, with the situation reportedly influenced by the leasing activity of a major streaming service within the portfolio.

data_points.project_notes: Loan transferred to special servicing amid agreed extensions and impact from a major streaming service's leasing.
